summary: Adopted the concurrency primitives so workers actually USE them. PART A (CAS claim): daemon.js /overlay/status now has a claim-steal guard — a claim (->in_progress with agent_id) is refused 409 if the task is already in_progress under a DIFFERENT assignee (re-claim by same agent = no-op; force:true = explicit takeover). Canceled-claim refusal already existed (terminal guard). start_task MCP tool gained force passthrough + CAS doc. PART B (enforced cooperative-stop): added GET /should-stop?session= (maps session->in_progress task->agent via buildGraph, returns stop:true if cancel_requested[task] OR stop_requested[agent]) and a sibling PreToolUse hook hooks/orch-stop.sh wired matcher:"*" in hooks.json BEFORE the Write|Edit edit-gate — denies any tool call with exit 2 + 'STOP: cancellation/stop requested — halt and report'. Preserves ORCH_GATE_OFF, sessions/<id>.off, daemon-unreachable fail-open. PART C: smoke.sh +10 assertions (claim-canceled refused, fresh-claim ok, double-claim refused, re-claim-same ok, force takeover, should-stop clean/flagged, hook exit0 normal + exit2 STOP message). Verified live via curl (double-claim 409, canceled 409, force takeover) and hook stdin tests. smoke 38/38, node unit tests 3 suites green. Daemon restarted by exact PID (now 55624), workspace re-registered, my claim CAS-held not stolen. CONCURRENCY: another worker (sub-escalation/#11, self-learn-planner) edited lib/overlay.js, public/graph.html, skills/ in parallel — left intact, not clobbered. FOLLOW-ON: the self-scheduling loop (#12) MUST also poll cancel_requested+stop_requested (or call /should-stop) and exit when built — the hook only gates tool calls, not an in-process heartbeat.
